test_title: PYST 68: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What distinguishes rough ER (RER) from smooth ER (SER)?

options.text: Absence of proteins in RER, presence in SER
Absence of membranes in RER, presence in SER
Presence of ribosomes on RER, absence on SER
Presence of chlorophyll on RER, absence on SER

solution:
The correct answer is __**Presence of ribosomes on RER, absence on SER**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** is a large, dynamic structure that serves many roles in the cell including **calcium storage**, **protein synthesis**, and **lipid metabolism**. It consists of a network of membranous tubules and flattened sacs called **cisternae**.
 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** is named for its rough, granular appearance under an electron microscope, which is due to the presence of **ribosomes** attached to its outer (cytoplasmic) surface. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** lacks these attached **ribosomes**, which gives it a smooth, tubular appearance. It is primarily involved in the **synthesis of lipids**, such as phospholipids and cholesterol.
 
• The **RER** is the site where **protein synthesis** occurs for proteins that are either secreted from the cell, incorporated into the cell's plasma membrane, or sent to an organelle like the **lysosome**.
 
• While **RER** is dominated by **cisternae** (flattened sacs), **SER** is largely composed of a network of **tubules** that are interconnected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of Rough ER:**
 
 
• It plays a central role in **protein folding** and **quality control**. Proteins that are misfolded are retained in the **RER** and eventually degraded.
 
• It is involved in **glycosylation**, the process of adding carbohydrate chains to proteins to form **glycoproteins**.
 
• The **RER** is continuous with the **nuclear envelope**, facilitating the transport of molecules between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Smooth ER:**
 
 
• In **liver cells**, the **SER** contains enzymes that catalyze reactions to **detoxify** drugs, metabolic wastes, and harmful chemicals.
 
• It is responsible for the **synthesis of steroid hormones**, such as estrogen and testosterone, in the reproductive organs.
 
• In **muscle cells**, a specialized form of **SER** called the **sarcoplasmic reticulum** regulates **calcium ion concentration**, which is vital for muscle contraction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Membrane Presence:** Both **RER** and **SER** are part of the **endomembrane system** and are composed of **phospholipid bilayers**. Therefore, saying membranes are absent in **RER** is factually wrong. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Protein Presence:** Both types of ER contain a variety of **enzymatic proteins** required for their specific metabolic activities. **SER** contains proteins for lipid synthesis, while **RER** contains proteins like **translocons** for ribosome docking. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Chlorophyll Location:** **Chlorophyll** is a pigment found exclusively within the **thylakoid membranes** of **chloroplasts** in plant cells and algae; it is never found in the **Endoplasmic Reticulum**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Lumen:** The internal space of the ER is known as the **ER lumen** or **cisternal space**. It is distinct from the surrounding **cytosol** and provides a unique environment for chemical modifications.
</ul
